events.text: Customer Product and Service Directory SD
1. What Is This Service Domain?

In BIAN v14.0, the Customer Product and Service Directory (CPSD) Service Domain maintains a consolidated directory — a catalog — of the most important details for the current products and services held by a specific customer.
Role: It acts as the master index or registry of customer holdings. It is the primary source for a customer 360 view of what products and services a customer owns.
1.1 Key Distinction

rows: Operational account balances — managed by Product SDs
Product instance references (account IDs) per customer
Contract terms and agreements — managed by Sales Product Agreement SD
Product metadata (type, name, status, version, features)
Customer profile master data — managed by Party Directory SD
Deep operational transaction data — managed by respective Product SDs
Lightweight eligibility reference for origination checks

events.text: Key Rule: CPSD stores lightweight reference data only. It does not duplicate operational data managed by Product SDs or contract data managed by Sales Product Agreement SD.
2. When to Use This Service Domain
Call the CPSD SD in any scenario requiring visibility of what products and services a customer holds, without querying the full Core Banking System.

rows: Customer applies for gold account requiring an existing Mortgage
Customer Offer SD queries CPSD to verify Mortgage product exists for Customer ID
Customer logs into mobile banking dashboard
App calls CPSD to get list of active product instance IDs for display
Relationship Manager reviews customer wallet share
Query CPSD to see full spread of products the customer owns
Orchestration layer registers Product BQ and publishes contract details

events.text: 2.1 During Origination (Eligibility Checks)
Scenario: A customer applies for a Gold status account which requires them to already hold a Mortgage.
Action: The Customer Offer SD queries CPSD to verify if a Mortgage product exists for that Customer ID. No need to query CBS directly.
2.2 During Servicing (Dashboard View)
Scenario: A customer logs into mobile banking. The app needs to display all their accounts (Loans, Cards, Savings) on the home screen.
Action: The app calls CPSD to get the list of active product instance IDs and associated metadata for the dashboard. A lightweight, fast query.
2.3 During Relationship Management (Wallet Share)
Scenario: A Relationship Manager needs to see the full spread of products a customer owns.
Action: They query CPSD to view the complete customer wallet share, including all product types and service holdings.
3. Level of Detail to Capture
CPSD is a Directory/Reference domain — not a processing domain. Data captured must be lightweight, not deep operational data.

rows: One CR record per product type
Savings Account Product, Current Account Product
One Product BQ record per account
Savings Basic Act 1, Savings Basic Act 2, Savings Premium Act 1
One CR record per service type
One Service BQ record per service

events.text: 3.1 Control Record (CR) per Customer
One CR record is created per customer, serving as the root directory entry. It captures:

items: Party involvement role and validity period.

events.text: 3.2 Product BQ — One Per Account Instance
A separate Product BQ record is created for each account instance a customer holds. Key fields:

items: ProductInstanceReference — account number and issuing authority.
ProductIdentification — TM Product ID, open/close dates.
ProductLifecycleStatus — current status with validity period (from/to).
ProductFeature — feature type, specification, name, and lifecycle status.

events.text: 3.3 Service BQ — One Per Service Instance
A separate Service BQ record is created for each service the customer has opted for. The structure mirrors the Product BQ pattern. Service BQ is planned for a future implementation phase.
4. When and How to Invoke
CPSD must be invoked once core confirms customer creation (new Customer ID received from CBS) and again whenever an account is provisioned or updated.

rows: Create directory entry; assert customer creation. Call immediately on new Customer ID from CBS.
Link customer to Account ID. Skippable if customer created without account.
Publish contract/parameter specifics from CBS; enables downstream display without querying CBS.

events.text: 4.1 Subsequent Lifecycle Update Triggers
The Product BQ Update endpoint must be called again on the following CBS events:

rows: PUT .../Product/{productid}/Update — update ProductFeature with new values
PUT .../Product/{productid}/Update — update status and ValidityPeriod ToDateTime
POST .../Register (CR only) — Product BQ registered later on account creation

events.text: 5. Proposed Changes to BIAN Specification
The following changes were applied to BIAN v14.0 to support practical implementation:

rows: Prevents recursive loop generation across multiple paths including EntryStatus, UsageLog, UpdateLog, EntryInstanceReference, CustomerReference, ServicerReference, and ServiceAgreementReference paths.
Enables 1 CR to hold many Product BQ records; real customers hold multiple accounts of different types.
Enables 1 CR to hold many Service BQ records; real customers may opt for multiple services.
Non-standard BIAN endpoint to return all CR and BQ details for a CustomerReference; required for Customer 360 view.
Non-standard BIAN endpoint to return BQ Product details for a specific ProductInstanceReference (account number).

6. Implementation Priority
Note: Endpoint 7 (CustomerProductServices/Retrieve by party reference data directory ID) requires further discussion before implementation.
7. Data Ownership & Persistence
The CPSD SD maintains its own database schema to store data in accordance with BIAN API payloads. This SD owns its data — it does not rely on CBS or other SDs for its stored data:

rows: CustomerProductAndServiceDirectoryEntry — status, validity period, CustomerReference (CIF), ProductAgreementReference
One record per account instance: ProductInstanceReference, ProductIdentification, ProductName, ProductType, ProductLifecycleStatus, ProductVersion, ProductFeature
One record per service instance (same structure as Product BQ): service reference, type, lifecycle status
ValidFromDate, ValidToDate, StatusReason for both CR and BQ records

events.text: 8. Related Service Domains & Systems

rows: Product SDs (Current Account, Savings Account, Loan, etc.)
Source of operational product data (balances, transactions). CPSD stores lightweight reference only; does not duplicate operational data.
Holds formal contract terms. CPSD references the agreement via ProductAgreementReference but does not manage agreement content.
Queries CPSD during origination for eligibility checks (e.g. verify Mortgage product exists before offering Gold account).
Authoritative source of customer profile master data. CPSD references customer via CIF (CustomerReference.PartyReference).
Primary consumers of CPSD; query it for the Customer 360 dashboard view and wallet share without hitting CBS directly.
